title: Converting area & volume units
examples: When converting area units, should I multiply or divide?
Is the relationship between cm cubed and litres always the same?
What if I have a mix of units in one problem?

explain.say: Today we learn to change area and volume units. We will look at square centimetres to square metres. Remember that one metre equals one hundred centimetres.
To change square centimetres to square metres, we divide by ten thousand. Think of it like this: one square metre is one hundred times one hundred centimetres. So we divide by ten thousand.
For example, if you have five thousand square centimetres, you divide by ten thousand. Five thousand divided by ten thousand equals zero point five square metres.
Next we look at volume units. We compare cubic centimetres to litres. The relationship here is quite simple to remember.
One cubic centimetre is exactly equal to one millilitre. Since one litre has one thousand millilitres, we divide by one thousand to go from cubic centimetres to litres.

faq.q: When converting area units, do I always divide by ten thousand?
faq.a: You divide by ten thousand when going from square centimetres to square metres. This is because one metre is one hundred centimetres, so one square metre is one hundred times one hundred centimetres.
asks: How do I change cm² to m²?
What is the rule for square centimetres to metres?

faq.q: Is the relationship between cm³ and litres always the same?
faq.a: Yes, the conversion is constant. One cubic centimetre is always equal to one millilitre. Therefore, you divide by one thousand to find the volume in litres.
asks: How many litres are in 1000 cm³?
What is the volume conversion factor?

faq.q: If I go from metres to centimetres, do I multiply or divide?
faq.a: You multiply by one hundred when going from metres to centimetres. Remember that one metre equals one hundred centimetres.
asks: How do I convert m to cm?

faq.q: Can I use the relationship between cm³ and ml for everything?
faq.a: You can use the millilitre relationship for volume. One cubic centimetre equals one millilitre. This helps you remember the division by one thousand for litres.
asks: Is ml the same as cm³?

faq.q: What if I have a measurement in square millimetres?
faq.a: For square millimetres, you would divide by ten thousand to get to square metres. You must be careful with the number of zeros.
asks: What is the area conversion for millimetres?

facts: One metre is equal to one hundred centimetres.
One square metre is equal to ten thousand square centimetres.
One cubic centimetre is equal to one millilitre.
One litre is equal to one thousand millilitres.

quiz.say: What is 45000 square centimetres in square metres?
quiz.why: You divide forty five thousand by ten thousand, which gives you four point five.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you only divide by one hundred instead of ten thousand.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you divide by one million instead of ten thousand.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you forget to move the decimal point correctly.

quiz.say: How many litres are in 600 cubic centimetres?
quiz.why: You divide six hundred by one thousand, which gives you zero point six litres.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you only divide by ten instead of one thousand.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you multiply by one thousand by mistake.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you divide by ten thousand instead of one thousand.

quiz.say: If a box has a volume of 2500 cm³, what is its volume in litres?
quiz.why: Dividing two thousand five hundred by one thousand gives you two point five litres.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you forget to divide at all.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you divide by one hundred instead of one thousand.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you divide by ten thousand instead of one thousand.
